summary.oneLiner: Timex Group India is a leading watch manufacturer and marketer with a diversified portfolio spanning mass, fashion, and luxury segments, anchored by the iconic Timex brand and supported by a strong manufacturing base in India.
summary.business: Timex Group India Limited designs, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive range of watches and wearables. Its portfolio addresses a wide consumer spectrum from entry-level to luxury, including its flagship Timex brand, fashion labels like Guess and Versace, and licensed brands. The company operates through a multi-channel network of trade distributors, e-commerce platforms, and its own retail presence, including the 'Justwatches' chain.

plants.role: Assembly of a wide range of timepieces from core quartz analog and digital models to automatic watches, intelligent quartz, activity trackers, and connected smartwatches; also serves licensed and OEM partners.

currentContext.strengths: Strong, diversified brand portfolio anchored by the iconic Timex brand and supported by global design and manufacturing expertise from a parent with over 170 years of leadership.|Extensive multi-channel distribution network including a dominant trade channel, growing e-commerce presence, and a transformed retail model including the 'Justwatches' acquisition.|Vertically integrated manufacturing capability at the Baddi facility, enabling quality control, OEM servicing, and production of a wide product range from analog to smartwatches.|Product-led differentiation and a calibrated premiumisation strategy, exemplified by the launch of the Swiss-made Timex Atelier collection, enhancing brand equity.
currentContext.strategies: Expand e-commerce and physical distribution channels through deepened engagement on leading platforms, scaling D2C brand websites, systematic expansion of trade points of sale, and strengthening presence in Tier II/III markets.|Drive product-led differentiation, premiumisation into higher-value segments, franchise-led portfolio development, collaborations, channel expansion, and portfolio diversification.|Sharpen Timex's digital-first engagement strategy and deploy focused marketing initiatives across the fashion and luxury portfolio, building 'Justwatches' as a unifying aspirational destination.|Fully leverage the Baddi manufacturing facility's advanced capabilities and explore avenues to optimise its capabilities for future growth opportunities.|Strengthen and invest in human capital and partner ecosystem to support long-term objectives.|The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy per Regulation 43A. No dividend was recommended on equity shares. Preference dividends were paid/recommended to clear accumulated unpaid dividends on cumulative redeemable non-convertible preference shares out of distributable profits. No amount was proposed to be transferred to General Reserve.|Manufacturing facility certified to SA 8000 and ISO 45001:2018, reflecting commitment to workplace safety, health, and employee well-being.|Zero discharge of waste outside plant premises; waste is either reused in processes or disposed of to registered vendors for recycling.|CSR is applicable as per Section 135 of Companies Act, 2013, with turnover of Rs. 798.58 crore and net worth of Rs. 111.28 crore.|Board-approved policies cover all nine principles of National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC), including Code of Conduct, Whistle Blower Policy, and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's manufacturing facility at Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, represents a key pillar of its operational strength. The facility is equipped with advanced technology and a skilled workforce, capable of assembling an extensive portfolio from core quartz analog and digital models to automatic watches, intelligent quartz, activity trackers, and connected smartwatches. The Company remains focused on fully leveraging this strategic asset and will continue to explore avenues to optimise its capabilities in support of future growth opportunities. No new capex projects, capacity additions, or expansion timelines are disclosed.
currentContext.mdna: Indian economy demonstrated resilience with real GDP growth of 7.6% in FY2025-26; FY2026-27 GDP projected at 6.9% assuming contained geopolitical risks.|Premium and luxury watch segments outperformed, driven by rising disposable incomes, premiumisation trends, and acceptance of watches as lifestyle accessories.|E-commerce and omni-channel retail expansion enhanced market reach across Tier II and Tier III cities.|Wristwatch penetration in India remains relatively low, providing significant headroom for market expansion.|Tier II and Tier III cities represent an important growth frontier driven by rising incomes, improving retail and digital access, and increasing brand awareness.|India's young demographic profile and expanding cohort of digitally enabled Millennials and Gen Z consumers expected to sustain demand.|Premiumisation trends and rise of aspirational consumers with higher disposable incomes expected to benefit branded, premium, and luxury watch segments.|Private label offerings expected to play a meaningful role by addressing value-conscious consumers and offering attractive margins to retail partners.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange and commodity price volatility
risks.note: Dependence on imported inputs exposes the Company to adverse currency movements, while sharp fluctuations in gold and silver prices can pressure margins in relevant product categories.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and external dependence
risks.note: Manufacturing relies on timely availability of components from domestic and international suppliers; any disruption in material flows could create short-term imbalances in production and fulfilment.

Global shift towards technology-enabled and fashion-driven wearables presents a risk to traditional analog watch categories, requiring a dual-track strategy of technology products and premium fashion/luxury portfolios.

Rapid growth in digital commerce and omni-channel retail is reshaping consumer buying behaviour; failure to adapt could impact market reach and competitiveness despite traditional trade remaining a major contributor.
OEM operations exhibit a degree of customer concentration, carrying risks of order volatility, margin compression, and operational strain.

risks.risk: Labour and workforce risk at Baddi manufacturing facility
risks.note: Labour-intensive assembly operations face risks related to availability and retention of skilled manpower, workforce mobility, potential labour disruptions, and intensified competition for technically skilled resources.
Proliferation of counterfeit products poses an ongoing threat to brand equity and consumer trust across the watch industry.
